relation: sheet 8 lies NORTH of sheet 10; shared street 22nd Street
overlap_description: Both plates draw the FULL 80-ft width of 22nd Street, so the seam is a genuine ~245-px-tall overlap band running the whole sheet width. Each plate draws the NEAR property line as real block frontage and the FAR property line as the outer rule of its own continuation boxes ('SEE SHEET No.10' along the bottom of sheet 8, 'SEE SHEET No.8' along the top of sheet 10). Measured: sheet 8 north property line y=3610.0+0.00171x, south property line y=3849.6+0.00449x (241.0 px apart at x=500, 247.7 px at x=2900); sheet 10 north property line y=96.70-0.00033x, south property line y=342.96+0.00031x (246.6 px at x=500, 248.1 px at x=2900). Nominal 80 ft = 242.1 px on sheet 8 and 243.7 px on sheet 10, so both plates draw the street within about 1.5% of its printed width. The overlap contains only roadway furniture - the 22nd St water main, three fire plugs, the street-name lettering and the three alley-main tees. NO building, block or lot is drawn twice, and no block number is repeated: sheet 8's bottom block row is 501 / 441 / 381 and sheet 10's top row is 502 / 442 / 382. The two plates span exactly the same lettered avenues, Av. D (Market E.) on the west through Av. G (Winnie E.) on the east, which is what makes the seam so well controlled in x.

rejected_candidates.feature: Blind template / NCC matching across the seam
rejected_candidates.reason: Not attempted, per the project brief - the overlap band is bare roadway with a repeating alley/avenue rhythm at 120-ft and 260-ft pitch, exactly the structure that produced confident wrong matches three times before on this project. Every feature here was read semantically first (printed avenue names, block numbers, pipe diameters, street and alley width labels) and only then measured.

notes:
METHOD. Every feature was identified from printed lettering first - the four vertical avenue names AV. D or MARKET E. / AV. E or POST OFFICE E. / AV. F or CHURCH E. / AV. G or WINNIE E., the block numbers 501/441/381 (sheet 8) and 502/442/382 (sheet 10), the width labels 80' on 22nd St, 70' on each avenue and 20' on each alley, and the 12" W.P. / 16" W.P. pipe labels - and only then measured. Measurement was done on darkness profiles of the untouched JPEGs with sub-pixel centroids, cross-checked against 8x-22x nearest-neighbour crops carrying a 1-source-pixel grid overlay drawn at known source coordinates (crops in output/qc/manual_crops/). Scripts: scripts/manual_crop_s8_s10.py, scripts/manual_profile_s8_s10.py, scripts/manual_vline_s8_s10.py, scripts/manual_seam_S8_S10_solve.py.

WHAT WAS SURPRISING. (1) Both plates draw the whole 80-ft roadway, not half of it. Each draws the far kerb as the outer rule of its own continuation boxes, and that rule sits within 1-2 px of where the printed 80' width puts the property line. That gives real control on BOTH kerbs from BOTH sheets, which is what makes the 14 corner points possible. (2) The dashed kerb line is the awning edge, 39.7 px (13.1 ft) inside the roadway - measured directly off 21st Street inside sheet 8, where both awning lines are drawn on a street printed 80'. Taking it for the property line would have moved the seam 40 px. (3) The S7|S9 playbook's water-main tees do NOT transfer to this seam in y. The tee identification is certain (the 12in-to-16in change is lettered at the same alley on both plates), but sheet 8 runs the 22nd St main 143 px south of the north kerb and sheet 10 runs it only 99 px south - a 45 px systematic that appears identically at all three tees. The tee x is still good to 1-5 px. (4) The block frontage and alley/avenue property lines are far better than expected: fitted over 800 px of block depth their residuals are 0.06-0.9 px, so the x half of every correspondence is essentially exact.

SCALE AND ROTATION, INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED. The raw x separations between matched vertical lines grow smoothly from +4.3 px at x~293 to +23.1 px at x~3090, implying sheet 10 is drawn 0.67% larger in x than sheet 8. The weighted similarity gives scale 0.99232 (sheet 10 -> sheet 8), i.e. 0.77% . The printed scale bars give 3.026 px/ft on sheet 8 and 3.046 px/ft on sheet 10, ratio 0.99343 - agreement to 0.11%. The rotation, +0.170 deg, is confirmed twice more: the mean slope of the twelve vertical block-face lines differs by 0.0037 rad (0.21 deg) between the plates, and the mean slope of the horizontal seam lines by 0.0031 rad (0.18 deg).

HOW TO READ THE RESIDUALS. rms_px 11.79 and max_px 45.56 are dominated by the single deliberately-downweighted water-main tee. Over the 14 block-corner and property-line-intersection points the fit is rms 2.37 px, max 4.45 px; adding the retained fire plug it is rms 2.85 px. No point exceeds 3x its stated uncertainty. Worst corner is the Av. F - Av. G alley west line at the north kerb, 4.45 px against a stated 3.0.

HONEST CAVEAT ON THE Y COORDINATES. The x of each correspondence is an independent measurement of a distinct printed line (13 distinct vertical lines). The y coordinates are NOT independent: they come from four straight-line fits to the two 22nd St property lines on each plate, sampled in 120-px windows across the full width (n = 20, 21, 21, 21; fit rms 2.04, 1.18, 1.45, 1.10 px). Straight lines were used deliberately, because the local +-2 to 3 px jogs in a block frontage are one draftsman's building line and are NOT shared with the other plate's continuation-box rule, so smoothing them out is more accurate than honouring them. The consequence is that the y information in this set carries roughly four degrees of freedom, not sixteen, and the seam therefore constrains relative y-scale much more weakly than relative x-scale. Sheet 8's two kerb lines are not quite parallel (slopes +0.00171 and +0.00449), so its drawn street width grows from 241.0 px at x=500 to 247.7 px at x=2900; sheet 10 is steadier at 246.6 to 248.1 px. That ~6 px divergence is the main reason the corner residuals sit near 2-3 px rather than below 1 px, and it is real drafting, not measurement error.

PRIVACY. All work local. No imagery left the machine, no external image API was called, no URL was created, nothing was committed or pushed.
